## Series Overview

Real defect examples are chronically scarce in industrial X-ray inspection -- especially for
rare defect classes like voids, cracks, and bent leads. The usual manual fallback is
cut-and-paste: crop a real defect, paste it into a good image. This series explores whether
there's something better, working through the space of synthetic-defect-generation methods
from first-principles physics to learned generative models, using the real, public
[GDXray](https://github.com/computervision-xray-testing/GDXray) dataset throughout.

Every post ends with an honest limitation, not just a win -- same ethos as the
[Local-AI Defect Inspection](../local-ai-defect-inspection/index.qmd) series, which this one
complements: that series evaluates and fine-tunes models on real defect data; this one is about
generating more of it. The [Video & Sound Generation](../video-sound-generation/index.qmd) series
picks up the same real GDXray data and asks the video+audio version of this question.

### Posts in this series

1. **Part 1** -- [Physics-Based X-ray Simulation](01-physics-based-xray-simulation.qmd). No
   imaging-equipment access, so every physical parameter is fit directly from real GDXray pixel
   statistics: an attenuation-depth calibration, a photon-noise model, a blur kernel -- then a
   real base radiograph is inverted, edited inside a mask, and re-rendered into a synthetic defect
   image with a ground-truth mask for the injected defect, free.
2. **Part 2** -- [Mask-Conditioned Diffusion Fine-Tuning](02-mask-conditioned-diffusion-finetuning.qmd).
   LoRA fine-tunes a real Stable Diffusion inpainting model on real GDXray defect crops, so it
   learns actual defect *texture* instead of physics's hand-drawn shape -- compared directly
   against Part 1 on the identical mask.
3. **Part 3** -- [ControlNet-Conditioned Diffusion](03-controlnet-conditioned-diffusion.qmd). Same
   SD1.5 setup as Part 2, plus a ControlNet fed the *real* defect silhouette instead of a synthetic
   crack shape -- confirmed real and measurably different from Part 2's output, but inconclusive
   on a single example whether it reads as more authentic; the real test is Part 9's downstream
   comparison.
4. **Part 4** -- [Flux-Based Mask-Conditioned Generation](04-flux-mask-conditioned-generation.qmd).
   Swaps SD1.5 for a 12B-parameter diffusion transformer (real, gated checkpoint -- access
   confirmed via the HF API first) -- a genuinely surprising, honestly-reported negative result:
   the bigger model was *less* visible than Part 2's on the identical test case.
5. **Part 5** -- [Joint Image and Mask Diffusion](05-joint-image-mask-diffusion.qmd). A
   from-scratch model trained to generate the defect image *and* its mask together, no
   conditioning at all -- directly inspired by NVIDIA's MAISI architecture, scoped to 2D. First
   run overfit with no warning from the loss curve; revised after a reader question surfaced a
   missing standard technique (EMA weight smoothing) -- real, better, still-imperfect results
   after adding it, still the weakest method in the series so far, but closer.
6. **Part 6** -- Combining what works. Takes whichever of Parts 3-5 actually helped, combines it
   with Part 1's calibrated noise model, and reports whether the improvements actually stack.
   Coming soon.
7. **Part 7** -- [GAN-Based Synthesis](07-gan-based-synthesis.qmd). A distinct third generative
   family: a from-scratch, defect-aware conditional GAN. The adversarial half broke almost
   immediately (the discriminator dominated by step 100 of 3000) -- exactly the failure mode
   this series' design spec predicted -- and the L1 reconstruction term alone produced a real,
   visible defect mark, but with an architecture-specific checkerboard artifact that inflates
   local texture variance *above* the real defect's own.
8. **Part 8** -- Cut-paste + Poisson blending baseline. Coming soon.
9. **Part 9** -- Post-training a real detector on synthetic data (the payoff). Post-trains the
   same baseline detector separately on real+synthetic splits from every method above, ablates
   the real:synthetic ratio, and reports which method's data actually moves a real downstream
   model. Coming soon.
